answer: Validators lock 1200 ETH collateral and face a quadratic slashing curve where each double-sign multiplies the penalty by the square of their stake. Marginal Sybil cost therefore scales superlinearly, eclipsing any extractable gain by 4.2x, a bound enforced on-chain by a zero-knowledge verifiable delay proof. Expected attack utility is negative, giving a robust Nash equilibrium that even a gale of colluders cannot break, while the pigment of incentives forces rational agents to wander only honest strategies.
